subject: Leaning Tower of Pisa
title: What If a Tower Leaned More Every Year? Pisa's Did, Until Engineers Dug Under It

scenes.text: What if a tower leaned a little more every year? Pisa's did, for eight centuries.
Building starts in 1173. Five years later, barely two floors up, it's already tilting on soft ground.
By 1990 the lean is so bad the tower is closed. Nobody is allowed up for over a decade.
The fix isn't pushing it back. Engineers hold it with steel cables and remove soil from under the high side.
The tower settles back by about 38 centimeters, roughly 15 inches. It reopens in December 2001.
It should now stand for at least 200 years. And it's still correcting itself: about four more centimeters since.

description:
What if a tower leaned a little more every year? The Tower of Pisa, begun in 1173 on soft ground with shallow foundations, started tilting five years into construction and kept going for eight centuries.
It was closed to visitors in 1990. Engineers steadied it with steel cables and removed soil from beneath the higher north side, letting it settle back by about 38 centimetres. It reopened in December 2001 and is expected to be safe for at least 200 years; it has since straightened about another 4 centimetres on its own.
What should we run through next?
